definition: A condition (also called collapsed lung or punctured lung) where air fills the space between your lung and chest wall (pleural space), pressing against the lung and causing it to partially or fully collapse.
general_symptoms: Chest pain on one side, especially when taking breaths
general_diagnosis_methods: Listening to lungs with a stethoscope
Imaging (chest X-rays, CT scans, lung ultrasound)
History of lung disease and physical exam
Diagnosis based on symptoms (for specific severe types like tension pneumothorax)
general_treatments: Chemical pleurodesis (using doxycycline or talcum powder)
Surgery (for persistent leaks, non-expanding lung, recurrent collapsed lung, or traumatic injuries)
general_outlook: Can be a medical emergency / life-threatening
Most of the time heals in a few days to two weeks
Most people heal without major treatment
complications: Damage or infection caused by treatment
prevention: Avoid or limit activities with drastic changes in air pressure (scuba diving, flying) or follow precautions
See provider regularly to monitor underlying lung conditions

causes: Abnormal air pockets in lung (blebs) breaking apart without underlying health conditions
Underlying lung diseases causing blocked lungs and bursting bulges (bullae)

subtypes_and_causes.mechanism: Caused by physical injuries or medical procedures.

causes: Medical procedures (nerve block, lung biopsy, central venous line placement/insertion, mechanical ventilation)

subtypes_and_causes.definition: A rare type occurring around the time of menstruation (period) in females who ovulate, mostly affecting the right lung.
specific_symptoms: Symptoms starting within a few days before or after the start of period
causes: Endometriosis (endometrium tissue growing in lungs, pleurae, or diaphragm)
Prostaglandins causing reduced blood flow and rupture of air pockets in lungs
Air moving through reproductive tract through small holes in diaphragm into pleural space
targeted_treatments: Video-assisted thoracoscopy (VATS) to remove endometrial tissue, fix diaphragm, or close blebs
Hormone-regulating medications (oral contraceptives, GnRH agonists, danazol)
Pleurodesis (attaching lung to chest wall chemically or by scraping pleura)
Hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy (removes uterus and ovaries to stop ovulation)
outlook: Often keeps coming back without treatment
Requires multiple treatment types (surgery and medications)

related_conditions.cause: Endometriosis spreading to lungs or structures around them
associated_complications: Coughing up blood around period (catamenial hemoptysis)

subtypes_and_causes.mechanism: Air enters lungs/pleural space but cannot get out, creating a one-way valve effect that causes dangerous pressure buildup.
outlook: Serious form of pneumothorax that is a medical emergency
diagnosis: Diagnosed primarily based on physical symptoms

lifestyle_risk_factors: Tall, thin body type (especially in men)
Flying involving drastic air pressure changes
